title: The role of multiprotein bridging factor 1 (MBF1c) in Funariaceae species under salt stress
author: Maria Victória Magalhães de Vargas

steps_raw.instruction: The experimental plants used in this study were Funaria hygrometrica Hedw., Physcomitrium acutifolium Broth., and Physcomitrella patens (Hedw.) Brunch & Schimp, as represented in Figure 6A, B, and C, respectively. The plant culture protocol methods were carried out according to the methods described by Reski et al. (1994). Two to three gametophytes were grown in KNOP (Reski & Abel, 1985) liquid medium, containing 250 mg/L KH2PO4, 250 mg/L MgSO4 × 7H2O, 250 mg/L KCL, 1000 mg/L Ca(NO3)2 × 7H2O, 12,5 mg/L FeSO4 × 7H2O, pH 5.8, under constant agitation.

The plants were grown in the medium for 7 days in a photoperiod greenhouse with 16 h/8 h light/dark at a temperature of 23 ± 1°C. After initial growth, the regenerated tufts were transferred to liquid KNOP medium supplemented with different concentrations of NaCl (200, 400, 600, and 800 mM) to obtain the same stages of development for all the plants. The plants were grown under the same conditions in both the 12 h and 24 h experiments. All plant and treatment experiments were performed in 4 replicates. After the salinity experiments, the samples were stored at ‒80°C until RNA extraction.

After the salinity experiments, the samples were subjected to total RNA extraction protocol using a PureLink™ RNA Mini Kit (Invitrogen, CA, USA). Briefly, <100 mg of plant tissue was used for extraction, according to the recommendations established by the kit. The extraction product was quantitated using a Qubit™ RNA HS Assay Kit (Invitrogen, CA, USA) with Qubit Fluorometric Quantitation (Thermo Fisher Scientific, CA, USA) kit.

The replicates of each treatment were pooled for further analysis. The samples were cDNA-transformed using a High-Capacity RNA-to-cDNATM Kit (Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA, US) and quantitated using a Qubit™ dsDNA HS Assay Kit (Invitrogen, CA, USA) by Qubit Fluorometric Quantitation (Thermo Fisher Scientific, CA, USA).

Samples were diluted with nuclease-free water (Promega) to standardize the amount of cDNA. The standard used was 20 ng of cDNA per millilitre. The qRT-PCR experiments were performed post-standardization using the GoTaq® qPCR Master Mix kit (Promega), a system consisting of a fluorescent DNA-binding dye, BRYT Green® Dye. The protocol was carried out according to the manufacturer’s instructions and run on Rotor-Gene Q (Qiagen). The PaMBF1c gene was analysed using the following primer pair: forward primer: 5'- CCGAACTTGCACAGAAGAT-3', reverse primer: 5'-GCGTCTGTTTACGAATTTACAC-3', as described by Alavilli et al. (2017). The expression was calculated by normalizing the expression values against those of the housekeeping gene, actin 2/8: forward primer: 5'- GGTAACATTGTGCTCAGTGGTGG-3',	reverse	primer:	5'- AACGACCTTAATCTTCATGCTGC-3'. The amplification protocol consisted of 2 min for GoTaq® Hot Start Polymerase Activation at 95 °C, followed by 45 cycles at 95 °C for 15 s, 60 °C for 1 min. The ΔΔCT method was used to calculate the expression levels (Livak & Schmittgen, 2001).

The P. patens MBF1 sequences were searched for in Phytozome 12.1.6 (Goodstein et al., 2011). The selected "Phypa_110138" sequence is an alias of the Pp3c10_13060 gene, which shares information with the transcription factor PaMBF1c. Using the GENEVESTIGATOR software (Hruz et al., 2008), investigations into the "Custom Physcomitrella all-gene-array" platform demonstrated the presence of perturbations co-related to the Phypa_110138 gene.

The heatmap assays and expression levels at different stages of Physcomitrella patens development were performed using the PEATmoss platform (Fernandez-Pozo et al., 2019). The reference genome used is the most recent and currently available gene annotation, v3.3 (Lang et al., 2018). ID Pp3c8_3310V3.1, Pp3c3_36750V3.1, and Pp3c10_13060V3.1 refer to the MBF1 copies of MBF1b, MBF1b, and MBF1a, respectively.
